```{python}
#| label: setup
#| echo: false
import os
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from PIL import Image

plt.rcParams.update({
    "figure.dpi": 110,
    "savefig.bbox": "tight",
    "axes.titlesize": 11,
    "axes.labelsize": 10,
    "font.size": 10,
})

ROOT = Path.cwd()
LOGS = ROOT / "logs" / "imagenet"
DATA_IMAGES = ROOT / "data" / "images"

def show(path, figsize=(10, 4), title=None):
    """Display a pre-rendered figure stored in the repo."""
    path = Path(path)
    if not path.exists():
        print(f"[missing] {path}")
        return
    img = Image.open(path)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
    ax.imshow(img)
    ax.axis("off")
    if title:
        ax.set_title(title)
    plt.show()
```

# Introduction

## Website overview

This website is the **reproducibility and deployment reference** for the
*Dynamic Vision Transformer* (Dynamic-ViT) pipeline originally implemented by
Gabriel François, Avner El Baz and Léo Leroy, inspired by
@rao2021dynamicvit and built on top of the standard ViT of @dosovitskiy2021vit.
It was then augmented with an MAE-style self-supervised stage [@he2022mae]
and a semantic alignment stage (REPA) distilling features from a frozen
DINOv2 backbone [@oquab2024dinov2].

The goal of this site is **not** to retrain the models from scratch —
training the full pipeline on ImageNet-1k requires a multi-GPU setup
that is incompatible with a Continuous Integration runner. Instead, this document:

- documents the project structure, its dependencies, and the configuration used;
- re-renders the figures and checkpoints produced by the training scripts so
  that readers can inspect the results without having a GPU;
- describes how to reproduce a **single forward pass** of the lightweight
  Student on any 128×128 RGB image, locally or from a fresh clone of the repo;
- acts as the public entry point for CI/CD (GitHub Actions auto-publishes
  this site on every push to the `reprod` branch).

::: {.callout-important}
## Caveats
- **Training** the Teacher and Student models requires a CUDA-capable GPU
  with at least ~16 GB of VRAM and several hours of compute — it is **not**
  re-executed when this Quarto report is rendered.
- All figures below are loaded from `logs/imagenet/` and
  `checkpoints/public/imagenet/`, which are produced by the training
  scripts under `src/train/`.
- The dataset (ImageNet-1k 128×128, `benjamin-paine/imagenet-1k-128x128`
  on Hugging Face) is public but heavy (~30 GB); the inference demo at the
  end of this report only needs a handful of sample images, bundled in
  `data/images/`.
:::

# Environment and dependencies

## Requirements

The code requires **Python 3.11+** and the dependencies pinned in
`requirements.txt` and `pyproject.toml`. A CUDA-enabled build of PyTorch is
strongly recommended for training; inference works on CPU.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### With `uv` (recommended)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/<your-org>/Vit-Pytorch.git
cd Vit-Pytorch
uv sync
source .venv/bin/activate     # on Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
```

### With `pip` + `venv`

```bash
git clone https://github.com/<your-org>/Vit-Pytorch.git
cd Vit-Pytorch
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate     # on Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

:::

A `.env` file is expected at the project root to redirect the Hugging Face
dataset cache (the raw dataset is gitignored):

```bash
# .env
HF_DATASETS_CACHE=path/to/your/dataset_cache
```

The most relevant dependencies, extracted directly from `pyproject.toml`:

```{python}

import tomllib

with open(ROOT / "pyproject.toml", "rb") as f:

runtime = pyproject["project"]["dependencies"]
dev = pyproject["dependency-groups"]["dev"]

deps = pd.DataFrame({

deps
```

## Hardware recommendation

| Component    | Training (full pipeline)                | Inference only               |
|--------------|------------------------------------------|------------------------------|
| GPU          | NVIDIA GPU, ≥ 16 GB VRAM (A100/V100/3090) | Not required (CPU works)     |
| CUDA         | 11.8 or 12.x                             | —                            |
| RAM          | ≥ 32 GB                                  | ≥ 4 GB                       |
| Disk         | ~50 GB for the cached ImageNet-128×128   | ~200 MB for checkpoints + code |
| OS           | Linux / macOS / Windows                  | Linux / macOS / Windows      |

The reference runs underlying the figures of this report were executed on a
single NVIDIA A100 GPU. Apple Silicon users can select the `mps` backend via
`--device mps`; it is slower but functional for small batches.

# Project structure

The repository follows a standard `cookiecutter`-like layout, with a clean
separation between **code** (`src/`, `helper_function/`), **configuration**
(`configs/`), **data plumbing** (`data/load/`), and **artefacts**
(`logs/`, `checkpoints/`). Raw data is *never* committed.

```text
Vit-Pytorch/
├── src/
│   ├── models/           # Architecture: ViT, DynamicViT, Patch Embed, Predictor LG
│   ├── train/            # Training loops: SSL teacher, REPA teacher, student
│   ├── test/             # Evaluation, FLOPs, MAE reconstruction quality
│   └── finetuning/       # LoRA fine-tuning scripts (STL-10)
├── configs/              # Hyper-parameters per dataset (ImageNet, CIFAR-10, STL-10)
├── data/
│   ├── load/             # HF dataset loaders (ImageNet, CIFAR, STL)
│   ├── raw/              # Local dataset cache (gitignored)
│   └── images/           # A few sample images for the website and inference demo
├── logs/                 # TensorBoard events and generated plots (committed)
├── checkpoints/
│   └── public/imagenet/  # Public .pth checkpoints served by this site
├── helper_function/      # LLRD, MAE helpers, colored logging, model loaders
├── .github/workflows/    # Quarto publish + Ruff CI
├── pyproject.toml        # Project metadata & dependencies (uv-compatible)
├── requirements.txt      # Pinned dependencies for pip
├── ruff.toml             # Linter configuration
├── _quarto.yml           # Quarto website configuration
├── index.qmd             # This report
└── LICENSE               # MIT License
```

The three main training scripts under `src/train/` (`train_teacher_SSL.py`,
`train_teacher.py`, `train_student.py`) correspond to the three stages
described in @sec-pipeline. The evaluation scripts in `src/test/`
(`compare_st-te.py`, `parameters_computing.py`, `test_SSLteacher.py`)
regenerate every figure displayed below.

# Scientific content

## Definitions

A Vision Transformer processes an image as a short sequence of patch tokens
rather than a dense grid. Given an image $I \in \mathbb{R}^{H\times W\times C}$
splitted into $N = HW / p^2$ non-overlapping patches of side $p$, the model
computes a sequence of $N+1$ $d$-dimensional tokens (including a learnable
`[CLS]` token) and applies $L$ transformer blocks on top [@dosovitskiy2021vit].

Three concepts are central to our pipeline:

- **Masked Autoencoder (MAE).** During stage 1, we randomly mask a large
  fraction $m$ of the patches (here $m = 0.75$) and train the Teacher to
  reconstruct the *normalised* pixels of the masked patches [@he2022mae].
  This yields strong **local** features without any labels.

- **REPA (Representation Alignment).** During stage 2, while fine-tuning with
  ImageNet labels, we additionally force an intermediate ViT layer to align
  with the features of a frozen DINOv2 backbone [@oquab2024dinov2]. The
  alignment loss is computed through a small MLP projection head and acts as
  a *semantic* bottleneck, distilling global structure into the Teacher.

- **Dynamic token pruning.** Following @rao2021dynamicvit, the Student
  (DynamicViT) inserts lightweight prediction modules ("Predictor-LG") at
  layers $\{4, 7, 10\}$. Each predictor outputs a keep/drop score per token;
  uninformative patches are progressively pruned, compressing the
  computation. The target cumulative keep ratio at layer $\ell_k$ is
  $\rho^k$, with base ratio $\rho = 0.7$.

The Student is trained with the composite loss from `src/train/dynamic_loss.py`:

$$
\mathcal{L}
  = \lambda_{\text{cls}}\,\mathcal{L}_{\text{CE}}
  + \lambda_{\text{kl}}\,\mathcal{L}_{\text{KL}}(s / T, t / T)
  + \lambda_{\text{distill}}\,\mathcal{L}_{\text{feat}}
  + \lambda_{\text{ratio}}\,\mathcal{L}_{\rho},
$$

where $\mathcal{L}_{\text{CE}}$ is the classification loss,
$\mathcal{L}_{\text{KL}}$ is a temperature-scaled Kullback–Leibler divergence
between the Student logits $s$ and the Teacher logits $t$ [@hinton2015distillation],
$\mathcal{L}_{\text{feat}}$ distills token-wise features on the *surviving*
tokens, and $\mathcal{L}_{\rho}$ penalises deviations from the target keep
ratios.

## Data used

All experiments target **ImageNet-1k at 128×128** resolution, loaded from the
Hugging Face hub dataset `benjamin-paine/imagenet-1k-128x128` through
`data/load/imagenet_loader.py`. The loader:

1. downloads (once) the train/validation splits into the `HF_DATASETS_CACHE`
   directory specified in `.env`;
2. applies a `RandomResizedCrop(128, scale=(0.7, 1.0))` + horizontal flip +
   ImageNet normalisation on the training set, and a plain resize +
   normalisation on validation/test;
3. splits the official train split into 90 % train / 10 % validation using
   a fixed seed (`generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(50)`), so the
   split is deterministic across machines.

A few samples are bundled under `data/images/` so the site can render
thumbnails without touching the Hugging Face hub:

```{python}
#| label: fig-samples
#| fig-cap: "A few training samples from `data/images/`. The number in the filename is the integer ImageNet class id."
sample_files = sorted(DATA_IMAGES.glob("sample_*.png"))

if sample_files:
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(sample_files), figsize=(14, 3))
    if len(sample_files) == 1:
        axes = [axes]
    for ax, img_path in zip(axes, sample_files):
        ax.imshow(Image.open(img_path))
        label = img_path.stem.replace("sample_", "")
        ax.set_title(f"class id: {label}", fontsize=9)
        ax.axis("off")
    plt.suptitle("ImageNet-1k 128×128 — a few samples", fontweight="bold")
    plt.show()
else:
    print("No sample image found in data/images/")
```

To make the tokenisation step tangible, we can split one of these samples
into the same 16×16 patch grid that the ViT actually sees, and then display
what a random 75 % MAE mask looks like:

```{python}
#| label: fig-patch-mask
#| fig-cap: "Left: the original image. Center: the 8×8 patch grid used by the Teacher (128/16 = 8 patches per side). Right: a random 75 % MAE-style mask applied at the *patch* level — this is the actual input the SSL Teacher is trained to reconstruct."

rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=0)
patch = 16
img_path = sample_files[0] if sample_files else None

if img_path is not None:
    raw = np.asarray(Image.open(img_path).convert("RGB"))

    # Some sample_*.png were generated via matplotlib and may include
    # white margins/title text ("Label: ..."). We crop back to the
    # dense image area before tokenisation visualisation.
    non_white = (raw < 245).any(axis=2)
    row_density = non_white.mean(axis=1)
    col_density = non_white.mean(axis=0)

    dense_rows = np.where(row_density > 0.50)[0]
    dense_cols = np.where(col_density > 0.50)[0]

    if dense_rows.size > 0 and dense_cols.size > 0:
        y0, y1 = dense_rows[0], dense_rows[-1] + 1
        x0, x1 = dense_cols[0], dense_cols[-1] + 1
        cropped = raw[y0:y1, x0:x1]
        if cropped.size > 0:
            raw = cropped

    img = np.asarray(Image.fromarray(raw).resize((128, 128)))
    H, W, _ = img.shape
    nh, nw = H // patch, W // patch

    grid = img.copy()
    for i in range(1, nh):
        grid[i * patch - 1 : i * patch + 1, :, :] = 255
    for j in range(1, nw):
        grid[:, j * patch - 1 : j * patch + 1, :] = 255

    n_tokens = nh * nw
    keep_mask = rng.random(n_tokens) >= 0.75
    masked = img.copy()
    for k, keep in enumerate(keep_mask):
        if keep:
            continue
        i, j = divmod(k, nw)
        masked[i * patch : (i + 1) * patch, j * patch : (j + 1) * patch] = 128

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12, 4))
    for ax, im, title in zip(
        axes,
        [img, grid, masked],
        ["Original 128×128", f"{nh}×{nw} patch grid", "MAE mask (75%)"],
    ):
        ax.imshow(im)
        ax.set_title(title)
        ax.axis("off")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
```

## Training pipeline {#sec-pipeline}

The pipeline is a three-stage *hierarchical feature distillation* scheme:

1. **Stage 1 — SSL pre-training (`train_teacher_SSL.py`).** A ViT-Base
   Teacher is trained with an MAE objective on 75 %-masked patches, with a
   *decreasing* layer-wise learning-rate decay to prioritise early layers
   and capture **local** textures.
2. **Stage 2 — Supervised + REPA fine-tuning (`train_teacher.py`).** The
   SSL Teacher is fine-tuned with ImageNet labels, while an intermediate
   layer is aligned with frozen DINOv2 features through a small MLP head
   and a cosine similarity loss. Layer-wise learning-rate decay is now
   *increasing*, prioritising deep layers and the classification head.
3. **Stage 3 — Student distillation + dynamic pruning
   (`train_student.py`).** A DynamicViT Student is initialised from the
   Teacher's weights and trained with the composite loss defined above.
   Predictor modules at layers 4, 7, 10 learn which tokens to drop so that
   the per-image compute decreases while classification accuracy is
   preserved as much as possible.

The layer-wise learning-rate policy is intentionally asymmetric across stages.
For the supervised ViT phase (Teacher with REPA, then Student distillation),
we use an **increasing** layer-wise schedule: deeper blocks and the head get
larger updates, which helps adapt high-level semantic features to the target
classes. For the SSL MAE Teacher stage, we use a **decreasing** schedule so
earlier layers receive comparatively larger updates, encouraging robust local
texture and patch-level representations before semantic fine-tuning.

Running the full pipeline from the project root:

```bash
python -m src.train.train_teacher_SSL  --dataset imagenet --mask_ratio 0.75
python -m src.train.train_teacher      --dataset imagenet \
    --resume-from checkpoints/imagenet/ssl_teacher/ssl_teacher_best.pth
python -m src.train.train_student      --dataset imagenet --rho 0.7 \
    --run_name tiny_dynamic_vit
```

### Stage 3 — Student DynamicViT

The Student is optimised with four simultaneous objectives. Their individual
evolution across training is logged separately:

```{python}
#| label: fig-student-curves
#| fig-cap: "Stage 3: Student training curves. Top row: total loss and accuracy. Middle row: KL divergence with the Teacher logits (left) and feature-distillation loss on surviving tokens (right). Bottom row: ratio (sparsity) loss and the *effective* cumulative keep rate ρ produced by the Predictor-LG modules."
student_graphs = LOGS / "student" / "Student_ViT_imagenet1k-graphs"

panels = [
    ("student_loss_curve.png",      "Total student loss"),
    ("student_accuracy_curve.png",  "Student train/val accuracy"),
    ("student_kl_loss.png",         "KL divergence loss"),
    ("student_distill_loss.png",    "Feature distillation loss"),
    ("student_ratio_loss.png",      "Ratio (sparsity) loss"),
    ("student_rho.png",             "Effective cumulative ρ"),
]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(12, 12))
for ax, (fname, title) in zip(axes.ravel(), panels):
    p = student_graphs / fname
    if p.exists():
        ax.imshow(Image.open(p))
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.axis("off")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Configuration used

Stage-wise hyper-parameters live under `configs/`. Committing them to Git
guarantees that each run is reproducible from a single file. Below is a
programmatic dump of the ImageNet configuration, these are the exact
numbers that produced the figures above:

```{python}
#| label: tbl-config
#| tbl-cap: "Configuration `configs/train_imagenet1k.py` (ImageNet-1k 128×128)."
import runpy
cfg_raw = runpy.run_path(str(ROOT / "configs" / "train_imagenet1k.py"))
cfg = {k: v for k, v in cfg_raw.items() if not k.startswith("_") and not callable(v)}

categories = {
    "Architecture": ["d_model", "n_classes", "img_size", "patch_size", "n_channels", "n_heads", "n_layers"],
    "Optimisation": ["batch_size", "epochs", "alpha", "layer_decay"],
    "DynamicViT":   ["pruning_index", "rho", "rho_init", "steepness",
                     "lambda_class", "lambda_kl", "lambda_ratio", "lambda_distill"],
    "Normalisation": ["mean_norm_imagenet", "std_norm_imagenet"],
    "Fine-tuning":  ["finetuning", "rank"],
    "REPA":         ["lambda_repa"],
}

rows = []
for section, keys in categories.items():
    for k in keys:
        if k in cfg:
            rows.append({"section": section, "parameter": k, "value": str(cfg[k])})

pd.DataFrame(rows)
```

Secrets (Hugging Face tokens, data paths) are loaded at runtime from a local
`.env` file through `python-dotenv` and are **never** committed to Git.

## Reproducibility of our code and experiments

We followed the main principles of reproducibility in scientific research for Machine Learning:

- **Deterministic train/val split.** The 90/10 split is performed with
  `torch.Generator().manual_seed(50)` in `data/load/imagenet_loader.py`,
  so two different machines produce the exact same split.
- **Pinned dependencies.** `requirements.txt` lists every transitive
  dependency with an exact version; `uv.lock` plays the same role for the
  `uv` resolver.
- **Versioned configuration.** All hyper-parameters are Python modules
  under `configs/`, versioned alongside the code. Changes to these files
  are visible through `git blame` / `git log`.
- **Versioned checkpoints.** A curated subset of trained weights is
  committed to `checkpoints/public/imagenet/` (SSL Teacher, Teacher, and
  Student at $d_{\text{model}} = 128$, $p = 16$), so that any reader can
  bypass training and run inference directly.
- **Versioned artefacts.** The TensorBoard event files, loss curves and
  pruning visualisations displayed in this report live under `logs/` and
  are part of the repository, hence the figures above are regenerated by
  the CI at every push.
- **Continuous deployment/publication.** A GitHub Actions workflow
  (`.github/workflows/quarto.yml`) renders this `.qmd` on every push to
  the `reprod` branch and publishes the result to GitHub Pages.

# Inference on a custom dataset (for new experiments)

::: {.callout-note}
This section documents the *contract* that a user must respect to push a new
image through the trained Student. Because Quarto renders this page in a CI
environment without a GPU, we do **not** execute the forward pass live — we
describe the pre-processing, checkpoint loading and inference code a user
can paste into a notebook.
:::

## Input data specification and output format

- **Input.** A single image (PIL, NumPy or Torch tensor) with three RGB
  channels, **any** resolution. The preprocessing pipeline will resize it
  to 128×128 and standardise it with the ImageNet statistics used during
  training.
- **Output.** A Python dictionary:
  - `logits`: `torch.Tensor` of shape `(1, 1000)` — raw class scores over
    ImageNet-1k.
  - `top5`: a list of `(class_id, probability)` pairs, sorted by
    probability, with class ids matching the ImageNet-1k ordering.
  - `keep_masks`: a list of three binary masks (one per pruning index)
    of shape `(1, N)` with $N = (128/p)^2$ tokens. Useful to visualise
    which regions the Student actually looked at.

## Pre-processing pipeline

The same `torchvision` transforms used at test time (see
`data/load/imagenet_loader.py`) must be applied:

```python
from torchvision import transforms as T

IMAGE_SIZE = 128
MEAN = [0.485, 0.456, 0.406]
STD  = [0.229, 0.224, 0.225]

preprocess = T.Compose([
    T.Resize((IMAGE_SIZE, IMAGE_SIZE)),
    T.ToTensor(),
    T.Normalize(mean=MEAN, std=STD),
])
```

## Running a forward pass

```python
import torch
from PIL import Image

from src.models.dynamicViT import DynamicVisionTransformer

# 1. Load the public Student checkpoint shipped with this repo.
ckpt_path = "checkpoints/public/imagenet/d128patch16/student/student_epoch_120.pth"
ckpt = torch.load(ckpt_path, map_location="cpu")

# 2. Rebuild the exact architecture the checkpoint was trained with.
#    Hyperparameters are persisted inside the .pth by train_student.py.
student = DynamicVisionTransformer(**ckpt["hyperparameters"])
student.load_state_dict(
    {k.replace("_orig_mod.", ""): v for k, v in ckpt["model_state_dict"].items()},
    strict=False,
)
student.eval()

# 3. Run on a new image.
img = Image.open("data/images/sample_7.png").convert("RGB")
x   = preprocess(img).unsqueeze(0)                 # (1, 3, 128, 128)

with torch.inference_mode():
    logits, _feats, keep_masks, _scores = student(x)

probs   = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
top5_p, top5_i = probs.topk(5)
print(list(zip(top5_i[0].tolist(), top5_p[0].tolist())))
```

The returned `keep_masks` can be overlaid on the input to reproduce the
style of visualisation shown in @fig-pruning.

## Running the same inference in Docker

Docker packages the code, Python dependencies and runtime setup in an
isolated container, so the forward-pass demo runs the same way across machines
without local environment drift. In this repository, `Dockerfile` and
`compose.yaml` are configured to execute the Student inference workflow
reproducibly from a clean environment, which is useful for quick validation
or sharing the demo setup with teammates.

# CI/CD

## GitHub Actions workflow

Two workflows live under `.github/workflows/`:

- **`quarto.yml`** — renders this report with Quarto on every push to the
  `reprod` branch, then publishes the resulting static site to the
  `gh-pages` branch. The build installs dependencies with `uv sync`, so
  the CI uses the exact same lockfile as contributors.
- **`ruff.yml`** — runs the `ruff` linter/formatter on every push and PR
  to `main`, using the configuration in `ruff.toml` (88-char line length,
  double quotes, imports sorted).

## Tests

The `src/test/` directory acts as a small integration-test suite that can
be run manually after training:

- `parameters_computing.py` — loads both checkpoints and computes the exact
  FLOPs, MACs and parameter counts with `calflops`.
- `compare_st-te.py` — evaluates Teacher and Student on the ImageNet-1k
  test split, then regenerates the performance and confusion-matrix
  figures displayed above.
- `test_SSLteacher.py` — reports MSE, MAE and PSNR for the MAE Teacher and
  re-renders the `ssl_reconstruction_*.png` visualisations.

A light-weight `pytest` entry point is declared in `pyproject.toml`
(`[scripts] test = "pytest"`) for future unit tests targeting the
model building blocks.
